"Create a fully playable 3D cartoon-style obstacle-course competition game inspired by the classic Wipeout TV show and console games.

CORE GAMEPLAY:
Build a round-based obstacle-course competition where the player controls a character and must survive increasingly difficult obstacle courses. The competition must progress through multiple rounds, with the final round always called WIPEOUT ZONE. Players must physically control their characters throughout the entire game. The game must NEVER play itself.

ROUND STRUCTURE:

1. Qualifier – Big Red Balls, balance beams, slippery platforms and moving obstacles.
2. Sweeper Challenge – rotating sweepers, jumping platforms and moving hazards.
3. Dizzy Zone – spinning platforms, swinging obstacles and difficult balance challenges.
4. WIPEOUT ZONE – a massive final obstacle course combining multiple obstacle types, difficult jumps, moving hazards and a final finish platform.

Include qualification systems, elimination, checkpoints, timers, leaderboards and results screens.

CHARACTER SELECTION:
Create at least 20 different selectable cartoon characters with different body shapes, heights, weights and physical attributes. Include tall skinny characters, short chunky characters, heavy characters, muscular characters, athletic characters and lightweight characters.

Each character must have individual stats for speed, jumping, balance, strength, stamina and recovery. These stats must genuinely affect gameplay. Characters must have unique appearances, animations and personalities. Include unlockable characters and character customisation.

OBSTACLE LIBRARY:
Include giant Big Red Balls, rotating sweeper arms, swinging hammers, surprise punching obstacles, slippery ramps, collapsing platforms, moving walls, rotating cylinders, balance beams, launch pads and other creative obstacle challenges.

Obstacles must have functional physics and proper collision detection.

PHYSICS AND ANIMATIONS:
Implement funny, exaggerated ragdoll physics. Characters must stumble, fall, bounce, slide, tumble, get knocked backwards and fly into the water. Include recovery animations when getting back up. Falling into water must trigger proper splash effects and a respawn or checkpoint system.

ARENAS:
Create multiple visually distinct 3D competition environments, including Classic Wipeout Arena, Tropical Island, Winter Wipeout, Desert Arena, Nighttime Stadium and Extreme Industrial Arena. Each arena must have unique scenery, obstacle arrangements and visual effects.

GAME MODES:
Include Career Mode, Quick Play, Championship, Time Trial and Endless Wipeout. Build progression with unlockable characters, costumes, celebrations and rewards.

VISUAL STYLE:
Use colourful, exaggerated, polished 3D cartoon graphics. Characters, obstacles, arenas, water, scenery and menus should have proper 3D models. Avoid realistic graphics and avoid making the game look like a 2D mobile game.

CAMERA AND CONTROLS:
Use a third-person camera that follows the player's character closely while keeping upcoming obstacles visible. Include responsive mobile touchscreen controls for movement, jumping, sprinting and diving. Controls must be comfortable on mobile devices.

IMPORTANT:
Prioritise actual playable gameplay over menus and decorative features. Build fully functional courses, working obstacles, character physics, collision detection, round progression and a proper Wipeout Zone finale. Do not create fake buttons, placeholder obstacles or automated gameplay. Optimise performance for mobile devices.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

Architecture:
- Vite vanilla JS + three

- ui.js menus (DOM overlays) with character select, mode select, results, leaderboard

I'll implement: W/S forward/back, A/D strafe (camera-relative), Space jump, Shift sprint, X/C dive. Mobile: virtual joystick left, jump/sprint/dive buttons right. Camera follows behind player with yaw fixed toward course direction, staying 8-10 units back, 4.5 up, with lookahead.

Physics: player as a sphere/capsule on top of platforms; gravity, ground detection via ray against platform list; obstacles collision:
- Balls: sphere-push, big red balls rolling/bouncing; if touched while on platform, knock player.
- Sweeper arms: rotating horizontal beams, box collision -> knockback + tumble.

Player states: run, jump, stumble, knocked (ragdoll spin), falling, splash, recover, finished. Lives / respawn at checkpoint after splash with penalty.

Round structure: 4 rounds; fail => eliminated unless qualification? Include qualifier system: need to finish within time / among AI rivals? Add AI rivals as simple bots that follow course and can be knocked. Leaderboard ranks player vs bots. Elimination: if player splashes too many times (e.g. 3) or time expires, eliminated. To keep it fun, generous.

Course generation: procedurally constructed per round & arena with deterministic seed, themed visuals. Each round has segments with obstacles. Arena variants choose backdrop theme.

Round 1 qualifier: big balls, beams, slippery, moving obstacles.
Round 2 sweeper: rotating sweepers, jump platforms, moving hazards.
Round 3 dizzy: spinning platforms, swinging hammers, balance.
Round 4 Wipeout Zone: all combined, gaps, finish.

Settings include difficulty.

Let me design gameplay concretely to ensure it works.

Coordinate system: Course runs along -Z from start z=0 to finish z=-length. Player starts at z=2 facing -Z. Platforms segments defined as boxes with top y level (mostly 0). Water at y=-3.5. Platforms have center (x,z), size (w,d), top Y. Gaps between segments create jumping challenges. Checkpoints at z positions where respawn.

Course layout: total length maybe 220-320 units for round 4. Segment sequence with width 14 (arena). Player movement speed ~ 9 units/s base with stats speed factor 0.85-1.25 and sprint 1.5. Round lasts 60-120 sec.

Build course from "sections", each section ~24-40 units deep:
- flat platform with obstacles
- ball section: red balls rolling toward player (spawn periodically at far end, roll +Z), placed across path
- sweeper section: rotating arm around center pivot at platform level, arm length 8, rotates horizontally at ~1 rev/3s; must jump or duck? Jump over arm — arm lower, jump clears.
- beam section: narrow beam width 2.2 over water with swinging hammers
- slippery ramp: tilted platform with low friction, sliding sideways? keep simple: sloped platform, friction low so acceleration slides; plus push walls.
- collapsing platforms: tiles that disappear in sequence, need run through quickly.
- punching gloves: box glove pulses out from side at intervals.
- moving walls: barriers oscillating across the path.
- rotating cylinders: horizontal cylinder rotating about Z? Roll across width; collision pushes.
- launch pad: pad that launches player forward/up big.
- gap jumps: platform gaps requiring jump.
- finish platform wide with banner.

Collision design:
Player capsule approximated by sphere at feet center (radius 0.45, height 1.7). Ground: determine platform under player via AABB XZ and top Y near feet within step threshold. Use "highest platform top <= feetY + 0.35 and > water" pick. For airborne, land when falling and feetY <= top and previous feetY >= top-0.2. Simpler: feet Y, groundY = max top among platforms containing XZ (and top <= feetY + 0.5). Apply gravity; if feetY < groundY: snap, grounded. If no platform: fall to water -> splash.

Platform edges: walking off edge -> fall. Good.

Slopes: implement ramps as platform with topY varying along z (height function) for visual slide. Might skip slopes for collision simplicity but need slippery ramps. Could model "slippery" as low friction zone, with slight incline visual? We can implement tilted quads as top plane; ground height computed by plane equation. Add `slope` property {dir, amount} topY = baseY + amount * (position along dir normalized). Then physics slides. Hmm adds complexity but doable: groundAt(x,z) computes top for each platform where within bounds, including slope. Landing/ground snap works. Movement friction reduced in slippery zone via platform.slippery.

For platform gaps: course builder creates segments with gaps of 3-4 units; jumping distance at speed 9, jump vy=8, gravity 26 → airtime ~0.61s*9≈5.5 units. Fine.

Obstacle collisions: each obstacle gives colliders:
- sphere {type:'sphere', pos, r, vx,vz}
- box oriented around Y (sweeper arm): use closest point in local space; treat as capsule/cylinder horizontal at height. Compute player distance to rotating box; if within, apply knock.
- hammer: box at end.
Knock response: character enters 'tumble' state with random angular velocity, velocity impulse away, control reduced for ~1.1s, then recover at current spot if grounded. Hitting water while tumbling -> splash.

Ragdoll visual: character mesh group rotates (tumble) with limbs splayed; use procedural animation. Full ragdoll overkill. Use "cartoon ragdoll" tumble of the whole body + limbs flail. Good.

Splash: water particle burst, ring, camera shake, audio; respawn at last checkpoint after 1.4s with countdown and penalty +3s; splash count++. If splashes >= 3 => eliminated (results screen). Checkpoint pass increases respawn.

Timer: round time; HUD shows time, splashes, position, progress bar.

Qualification/elimination: need to finish. AI rivals times: assign target pace/arrival times; leaderboard at end with rank. If player eliminated, results screen "ELIMINATED" — but in career, should retry option. Include "Qualification" round: must finish top 6 of 8; since AI times fixed, player just needs finish before X time. Show qualifiers. Keep player's rank computed by progress among bots live.

Rounds progression: Career runs 4 rounds; each completion unlocks next round & rewards. If fail, retry round (no progress, maybe lose run). Championship: 4 rounds (each arena rotation, harder AI), points. Quick Play: single selected round. Time Trial: race clock, no eliminations, best time per course saved. Endless: start round 1 scenery, procedurally generated rounds with increasing speed until 3 splashes; leaderboard longest distance/rounds.

Character stats genuinely affect:
- speed: move speed, sprint
- jump: jump velocity, air control
- balance: recovery time, chance to resist knockback, beam stability (wobble)
- strength: knockback resistance, push obstacles, maybe punch objects away
- stamina: sprint duration/energy drain
- recovery: get-up time, splash penalty
Height/weight affect body scale, collisions (slightly), inertia and ragdoll.

Camera follows player: position = player pos + offset rotated by camera yaw. Auto-align yaw toward course (-Z) slowly, allow right-drag / touch drag to orbit? Sprint: stamina meter drains, speed boost 1.45x; regen when idle.

Balancing aspects: balance stat affects resistance to tangential drift and wobble (visual lean), and tumble.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D cartoon obstacle-course competition game inspired by Wipeout, including rounds, characters, obstacles, arenas, progression, and mobile controls.

## Requirements
- Fully playable third-person gameplay; no automated player control.
- Four-round structure ending with a course always named WIPEOUT ZONE.
- 20+ selectable characters with meaningful physical-stat differences, unlocks, and customization.
- Functional physics, obstacles, splashes, respawns, checkpoints, timers, leaderboards, elimination/result screens, and ragdoll-like movement.
- Career, Quick Play, Championship, Time Trial, and Endless modes.
- Multiple themed 3D arenas and mobile-optimized controls.

## Decisions
- Use Vite, Three.js, procedural 3D geometry, and WebAudio.
- Keep the game asset-light with generated characters, arenas, and effects.
- Implement characters and opponents as real rigs; opponents act as competitors rather than controlling the player.
- Use localStorage for progression and leaderboards.

## Work State
### Completed
- Scaffolded Vite/Three.js project and build scripts.
- Created 24-character roster with stats, unlock requirements, body variants, outfits, personalities, and procedural rigs.
- Implemented character physics metrics for speed, jump, balance, strength, stamina, recovery, knock resistance, and grip.
- Implemented obstacle classes for balls, sweepers, hammers, punches, ramps, platforms, walls, rollers, launch pads, and checkpoints.
- Implemented four course round types and six arena themes.
- Implemented environment, water, scenery, crowd, weather, and visual animation systems.
- Implemented player movement, jumping, diving, stamina, knockback, tumbling, splash respawns, and recovery.
- Implemented bot competitors, race positions, and championship planning.
- Implemented menus, roster, setup, HUD, results, standings, pause, touch controls, keyboard input, and local leaderboards.
- Implemented career/save/costume/token/character progression and audio synthesis.
- Started a local development server and performed browser smoke testing.
- Found and fixed a missing course-to-game-scene attachment bug.

### Active
- Final browser gameplay validation and visual tuning.

### Blocked
- No remaining technical blocker is recorded.
- Full end-to-end course completion and final visual polish still need verification.

## Next Move
1. Run `npm run build` and resolve any bundler errors.
2. Test Qualifier through WIPEOUT ZONE end-to-end in browser.
3. Verify checkpoints, splash respawns, finish ranking, results, unlocks, and round progression.
4. Recheck desktop and mobile camera framing and touch controls.
5. Save and inspect a final small JPEG smoke-test screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game.js`: Main game orchestration, modes, camera, race state, and course lifecycle.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/player.js`: Player movement, physics, stamina, obstacles, splashes, and recovery.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/course.js`: Round layouts, platforms, checkpoints, finish, and course construction.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/obstacles.js`: Obstacle collision and animation library.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/characters.js`: 24-character roster and gameplay-stat derivation.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/characterRig.js`: Procedural cartoon character meshes and animations.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js`: Arenas, water, scenery, atmosphere, and environmental effects.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/themes.js`: Arena themes, rounds, and game-mode definitions.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui.js`: Menus, roster, setup, HUD, results, standings, and touch UI.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/bots.js`: AI competitor timing and ranking.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/save.js`: Local progression and leaderboard persistence.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/input.js`: Keyboard and touchscreen controls.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/style.css`: Full responsive visual styling.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: App shell and UI structure.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/package.json`: Scripts and dependencies.

## Important Context
- Development server command: `npm run dev -- --port 3002`.
- Build command: `npm run build`.
- Game is exposed for browser automation at `window.__wipeout = { game, ui, save, input, audio, renderer, THREE }`.
- The course bug fixed by adding `course.group` to `scene`.
- The game uses a start-position and direction convention where forward/negative-Z progression is important.

"Create a fully playable 3D cartoon-style obstacle-course competition game inspired by the classic Wipeout TV show and console games.

CORE GAMEPLAY:
Build a round-based obstacle-course competition where the player controls a character and must survive increasingly difficult obstacle courses. The competition must progress through multiple rounds, with the final round always called WIPEOUT ZONE. Players must physically control their characters throughout the entire game. The game must NEVER play itself.

ROUND STRUCTURE:

1. Qualifier – Big Red Balls, balance beams, slippery platforms and moving obstacles.
2. Sweeper Challenge – rotating sweepers, jumping platforms and moving hazards.
3. Dizzy Zone – spinning platforms, swinging obstacles and difficult balance challenges.
4. WIPEOUT ZONE – a massive final obstacle course combining multiple obstacle types, difficult jumps, moving hazards and a final finish platform.

Include qualification systems, elimination, checkpoints, timers, leaderboards and results screens.

CHARACTER SELECTION:
Create at least 20 different selectable cartoon characters with different body shapes, heights, weights and physical attributes. Include tall skinny characters, short chunky characters, heavy characters, muscular characters, athletic characters and lightweight characters.

Each character must have individual stats for speed, jumping, balance, strength, stamina and recovery. These stats must genuinely affect gameplay. Characters must have unique appearances, animations and personalities. Include unlockable characters and character customisation.

OBSTACLE LIBRARY:
Include giant Big Red Balls, rotating sweeper arms, swinging hammers, surprise punching obstacles, slippery ramps, collapsing platforms, moving walls, rotating cylinders, balance beams, launch pads and other creative obstacle challenges.

Obstacles must have functional physics and proper collision detection.

PHYSICS AND ANIMATIONS:
Implement funny, exaggerated ragdoll physics. Characters must stumble, fall, bounce, slide, tumble, get knocked backwards and fly into the water. Include recovery animations when getting back up. Falling into water must trigger proper splash effects and a respawn or checkpoint system.

ARENAS:
Create multiple visually distinct 3D competition environments, including Classic Wipeout Arena, Tropical Island, Winter Wipeout, Desert Arena, Nighttime Stadium and Extreme Industrial Arena. Each arena must have unique scenery, obstacle arrangements and visual effects.

GAME MODES:
Include Career Mode, Quick Play, Championship, Time Trial and Endless Wipeout. Build progression with unlockable characters, costumes, celebrations and rewards.

VISUAL STYLE:
Use colourful, exaggerated, polished 3D cartoon graphics. Characters, obstacles, arenas, water, scenery and menus should have proper 3D models. Avoid realistic graphics and avoid making the game look like a 2D mobile game.

CAMERA AND CONTROLS:
Use a third-person camera that follows the player's character closely while keeping upcoming obstacles visible. Include responsive mobile touchscreen controls for movement, jumping, sprinting and diving. Controls must be comfortable on mobile devices.

IMPORTANT:
Prioritise actual playable gameplay over menus and decorative features. Build fully functional courses, working obstacles, character physics, collision detection, round progression and a proper Wipeout Zone finale. Do not create fake buttons, placeholder obstacles or automated gameplay. Optimise performance for mobile devices.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build and finalize a complete, playable 3D cartoon obstacle-course competition game inspired by Wipeout.

## Requirements
- Provide fully manual third-person gameplay across four rounds, with WIPEOUT ZONE always as round four.
- Include 20+ customizable characters, unlock progression, six arenas, career and alternate modes, physics, obstacles, checkpoints, leaderboards, results, and elimination.
- Support responsive keyboard and mobile touch controls with no automated player control.
- Prioritize playable courses and end-to-end round progression over decoration.

## Decisions
- Use Vite, Three.js, procedural geometry, and WebAudio.
- Use asset-light generated characters and environments.
- Persist progression and leaderboards in localStorage.
- Implement competitors as real bot rigs and never substitute them for player control.
- Forward movement progresses toward negative Z.

## Work State
### Completed
- Scaffolded Vite/Three.js project and production build scripts.
- Added 24-character roster, character stats, unlocks, body variants, costumes, and procedural rigs.
- Implemented movement, stamina, jumping, diving, knocks, tumbling, splashes, respawns, and checkpoints.
- Implemented obstacle, arena, course, bot, HUD, menu, results, progression, and audio systems.
- Added Career, Quick Play, Championship, Time Trial, and Endless modes.
- Added course attachment, ensuring `course.group` is part of the game scene.
- Verified `npm run build` passes successfully.
- Ran browser smoke tests for title, setup, countdown, racing, splashes, results, and mobile framing.
- Confirmed checkpoint and finish state transitions through automated position testing.
- Captured and inspected desktop and mobile screenshots.

### Active
- Final browser gameplay validation and visual tuning remain to be completed.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Complete a full uninterrupted player-controlled Qualifier-to-WIPEOUT-ZONE run.
2. Verify obstacle hits, all checkpoint respawns, qualification thresholds, round advancement, eliminations, finish ranking, unlocks, and leaderboard persistence.
3. Recheck desktop and mobile camera framing, touch controls, performance, and visual polish.
4. Save one final small JPEG viewport screenshot and inspect it.
5. Run a final production build after any tuning changes.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game.js`: Main race orchestration, modes, camera, state, and round lifecycle.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/player.js`: Manual movement, physics, collision response, stamina, and respawns.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/course.js`: Round layouts, platforms, checkpoints, finish, and course construction.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/obstacles.js`: Big Balls, sweepers, hammers, punches, ramps, walls, rollers, and launch pads.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/characters.js`: 24-character roster and gameplay-stat derivation.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/characterRig.js`: Procedural character meshes and animation rigs.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js`: Arenas, water, scenery, crowd, and weather.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/themes.js`: Arena themes, round definitions, and game modes.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui.js`: Menus, setup, HUD, results, standings, and roster.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/bots.js`: Competitor timing, ranks, and AI race rail.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/save.js`: Progression and local leaderboard persistence.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/input.js`: Keyboard and touchscreen controls.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/style.css`: Responsive HUD, menus, and touch styling.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/package.json`: Build and development scripts.

## Important Context
- The game is exposed at `window.__wipeout = { game, ui, save, input, audio, renderer, THREE }`.
- Browser smoke testing confirmed Qualifier can enter racing, fall for splash respawns, reach results, and complete finish-state transitions.
- Automated testing reached results for a teleported Time Trial run with rank 1 and `state: "results"`.
- The development server was last observed on port 3002, with an additional Vite instance on port 3003.
- Runtime build output is in `dist/`; source and project state remain uncommitted as untracked files.

## Objective
- Complete and finalize a playable 3D cartoon obstacle-course competition game inspired by Wipeout, with fully manual gameplay and a four-round finale named WIPEOUT ZONE.

## Requirements
- Support Career, Quick Play, Championship, Time Trial, and Endless modes; character customization and unlocks; six arenas; obstacles, physics, checkpoints, leaderboards, results, and eliminations.
- Use responsive keyboard and mobile touch controls; never automate player control.
- Prioritize playable courses and round progression over decoration.

## Decisions
- Use Vite, Three.js, procedural geometry, and WebAudio.
- Persist progression and leaderboards in localStorage; implement competitors as separate bot rigs.
- Forward movement progresses toward negative Z.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented the game systems, including 24 characters, multiple modes and arenas, obstacle courses, physics, progression, menus, HUD, and persistence.
- Verified `npm run build` passes and smoke-tested title, setup, countdown, racing, splashes, results, finish-state transitions, and mobile framing.
- Verified checkpoint and finish transitions with automated position testing.

### Active
- Final browser gameplay validation and visual tuning.
- A manually controlled Career run ended in elimination after three splashes; an attempted forward-plus-strafe input moved the player off the course.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue manual gameplay testing with centered forward input and deliberate steering; verify checkpoint respawns and round advancement through WIPEOUT ZONE.
2. Check qualification/elimination, finish ranking, unlocks, and leaderboard persistence.
3. Recheck desktop/mobile framing, touch controls, performance, and visual polish; save and inspect a final small JPEG screenshot.
4. Run `npm run build` after any changes.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game.js`: Race orchestration, round lifecycle, camera, and modes.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/player.js`: Manual movement, physics, collisions, and respawns.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/course.js`: Course layouts, platforms, checkpoints, and finish.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/obstacles.js`: Obstacle behavior and collision logic.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/input.js`: Keyboard and touchscreen controls.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui.js`: Menus, HUD, standings, and results.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/save.js`: Progression and leaderboard persistence.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/style.css`: Responsive styling and touch controls.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/package.json`: Build and development scripts.

## Important Context
- `window.__wipeout = { game, ui, save, input, audio, renderer, THREE }` exposes runtime state for browser validation.
- Browser smoke tests observed zero console errors and five warnings; production build had passed previously.
- The Career run started at `[0,0,8]` but after holding `w` and `d` reached `[11.10,-8.57,-0.10]`, took three splashes, and was eliminated. Further validation should avoid excessive strafe and inspect player movement/collision behavior.
- Repository files were untracked at last status check; no commit was made.
